name: Persian Joint Intent and Slot Filling Benchmark
description: Natural Language Understanding (NLU) is important in today's technology as it enables machines to comprehend and process human language, leading to improved human-computer interactions and advancements in fields such as virtual assistants, chatbots, and language-based AI systems. This paper highlights the significance of advancing the field of NLU for low-resource languages. With intent detection and slot filling being crucial tasks in NLU, the widely used datasets ATIS and SNIPS have been utilized in the past. However, these datasets only cater to the English language and do not support other languages. In this work, we aim to address this gap by creating a Persian benchmark for joint intent detection and slot filling based on the ATIS dataset. To evaluate the effectiveness of our benchmark, we employ state-of-the-art methods for intent detection and slot filling.
evaluation_method: accuracy (intent), token-level and entity-level F1 (slot filling), and sentence-level exact_match for joint predictions
general_score_metric: F1 (slot filling) — often reported alongside intent accuracy
reputation: A niche, recent benchmark targeting Persian NLU; limited adoption so far outside researchers working on low-resource intent/slot tasks.
notes: Derived from ATIS (English) for Persian — relatively small and domain-specific dataset; potential translation/coverage artifacts and limited domain diversity; not a large-scale LLM benchmark.
